How this works

method · coverage · caveats

Where the Glue spend goes

Cost Explorer stops at SERVICE and USAGE_TYPE: it knows Glue cost $5,968.69 over these 90 days, not which job spent it. This dashboard pushes through to the job. The run inventory comes from paginated GetJobRuns across all 195 jobs, topped up with 4,392 runs the API has already rolled off and the 2026-09-03 snapshot still held; 21,651 of 25,938 runs carry DPUSeconds, which is the figure AWS bills, so most of the attribution is measured rather than estimated. Coverage: 94.0% of billed DPU-hours land on a named job. The residual — 811.7 DPU-h, a median of 8.14 DPU-h per day — is spiky rather than flat, which points at billed work this attribution cannot see: a job deleted inside the period, or history the API dropped before the snapshot could catch it.

How the attribution works, and why it reconciles

Glue run history is not permanent, and it is not uniform. It dies with the job — delete a job and its cost stays on the bill while its history disappears — and for a job that runs every few minutes it also rolls off from the oldest end: adhoc-leads-bridge-pg-to-iceberg no longer returns anything before 2026-06-28, nine days into this window. Both gaps are filled here from the 2026-09-03 snapshot of this same dashboard, which recorded those runs while the API still served them. 21 jobs in that snapshot no longer exist at all (237.2 DPU-h inside the window).

How DPU is calculated

Where a run reports DPUSeconds, that value is used directly — it is what AWS bills. Otherwise it is DPU(worker) × workers × duration, using the worker configuration in force for that run and Glue’s 1-minute billing minimum.

Worker sizing: G.1X = 1 DPU, G.2X = 2, G.4X = 4, G.8X = 8. Cost throughout assumes $0.44 per DPU-hour, the rate confirmed from this account’s own bill (cost ÷ usage quantity on USW2-ETL-DPU-Hour: $5,898.98 ÷ 13,406.8 units). Since 2026-08-19 a second usage type appears on this bill, USW2-ETL-DPU-Hour-Gen2 at $0.308: 226.3 DPU-h for $69.71 over the window, 1.7% of Glue usage. Those hours are counted in the billed totals but priced at $0.44 like everything else, which overstates that slice by about $29.86.

The DPU-h / run column in the inventory averages each job’s last 20 billable runs — SUCCEEDED, FAILED or TIMEOUT. Failed runs bill, so they count.

Reading the inventory

Click any row for that job’s full run history — every recorded run with its cost, the triggers that start it, its configuration, and the errors it has thrown. History reaches back as far as Glue retains job runs, to 18 Sep 2025 on this account — but only for jobs that run rarely enough to keep it.

The Obs dot marks jobs with --enable-observability-metrics on. Those feed CloudWatch’s Glue namespace, which is billed separately as CloudWatch custom metrics — a per-metric monthly charge that does not appear anywhere in the DPU-hour figures above.

Runs marked reconstructed come from the 2026-09-03 snapshot, which built them from CloudTrail when their history had already left the Glue API. CloudTrail records that a run started and was billed, never how it ended, so their duration is a sampled median and their outcome is unknown.

What the bill cannot tell you

Runs that were billed and produced nothing $252.81

799 runs ended in FAILED, TIMEOUT or STOPPED and were billed anyway: 574.6 DPU-h. The worst is sessions-partners-prod at $90.22.

Glue triggers are not how work starts here 98.6% of runs

Only 1.4% of runs in this window were started by a Glue trigger, so the schedule behind each job lives outside Glue — Step Functions, Airflow, or a person. That is a reporting limit, not a problem: this data cannot tell you what cadence a job runs on, only that it ran.

Silent resizes 12 jobs

bookings-categories-etl-gold changed worker size 3 times inside the period (G.2X ×5 → G.4X ×5 → G.2X ×5 → G.4X ×5). Somebody is hand-tuning while it runs. This is also why a single DPU value per job misprices every run on the far side of a change — each run here is priced at the configuration it actually used.

History is shorter than the window 4,392 runs

GetJobRuns dies with the job and rolls off the busiest ones: 21 jobs from the previous snapshot no longer exist, and adhoc-leads-bridge-pg-to-iceberg has dropped everything before 2026-06-28. Those 4,392 runs were recovered from the 2026-09-03 snapshot — which is only possible because one was taken. Re-run this before the history ages out, or reconstruct from CloudTrail as references/service-deep-dive.md describes.
